attempts.outcome: HTTP 303 redirect to https://mic.eucast.org/. That page confirms there is NO downloadable compiled ECOFF file (Excel/CSV/PDF) and NO documented stable URL pattern for a single species+antibiotic result; the ECOFF is only rendered inside the interactive database graph.

attempts.outcome: TLS/CA failure on this host ('could not establish a secure connection'). An environment fault, not a EUCAST one.

attempts.outcome: No ECOFF value is stored anywhere in this repo. Every mention is a pointer to the aggregate EUCAST resource. `scripts/bvbrc_strict_mic_4drug_census.py` and `mic_tiers.py` both note only that tetracycline has 'no EUCAST breakpoints for E. coli (ECOFF only)' -- a statement about the clinical catalog, not a value.

explicitly_not_done: No value was written from memory. The search assistant volunteered 'the commonly cited 0.06 mg/L ciprofloxacin and 2 mg/L gentamicin ECOFFs' as a paraphrase; that is not a sourced quote and was NOT accepted.

No secondary source (e.g. an EFSA/ECDC summary report quoting EUCAST ECOFFs) was substituted. The plan specified EUCAST as the source, and the plan's third Open Question -- which EUCAST release to pin -- is still unresolved and is a user decision. Swapping the source class mid-execution to avoid a stall would be scope drift.

A human opens https://mic.eucast.org/search/, selects Escherichia coli and each agent, reads the ECOFF from the bottom-left of each graph, and pastes value + URL + verbatim quote into dna_decode/data/ecoff_catalog.py. Everything downstream is then already built and will run.

Resolve the open question of WHICH EUCAST release to pin first -- mixing releases across the ECOFF arm and the clinical arm would confound the very comparison the plan exists to make.
what_was_still_built: dna_decode/data/ecoff_catalog.py -- the catalog with the provenance contract enforced: a value cannot be added without a source_url and a verbatim_quote, and ecoff_for() RAISES rather than defaulting. This is the seam the values drop into.
dna_decode/eval/wildtype_tiering.py -- classify_wildtype(mics, ecoff) plus ecoff_is_resolvable_on_grid(), both pure and fully testable without any ECOFF value, since the cut-off is a parameter.

resolution.what_was_wrong_with_the_earlier_conclusi: The wall was real but MISDIAGNOSED. I concluded the EUCAST search was undriveable JavaScript. In fact the search IS addressable by query parameter -- my failing attempt used search[species]=1, which is simply the wrong id. E. coli is 261, and that id is published in plain HTML on EUCAST's own VetCAST page. Six attempts established that the values are not in TEXT; none of them tested whether the URL was addressable with a CORRECT id.
resolution.why_no_scrape_could_ever_have_found_the_: Each agent row links to /search/diagram/<id>, which serves a PNG. The ECOFF is RENDERED INTO THE GRAPH IMAGE, in its bottom-left corner, exactly as EUCAST's own documentation says ('shown in the bottom left-hand corner of each MIC and zone diameter graph'). So the values were read from the images themselves -- the primary source -- not from text, and not from memory.
resolution.reconciliation: Ciprofloxacin's 0.06 agrees across three independent reads: the all-agent results table (twice, different prompts) and its own diagram image.
resolution.one_suspicion_raised_and_cleared: Tetracycline reads 'ECOFF: 8 mg/L' beside 'Confidence interval: 2 - 4' -- an interval that does not bracket its own point estimate, which looked like a column misalignment by the page reader. Reading the graph directly EXONERATED the extraction: EUCAST prints exactly that. The interval describes the fitted wild-type distribution, not the cut-off. Do not 'correct' it.

ceftriaxone.note: printed in PARENTHESES = EUCAST's TECOFF marker (3-4 distributions)

resolution.manual_lookup_entry_point: https://mic.eucast.org/search/?search[method]=mic&search[antibiotic]=-1&search[species]=261&search[disk_content]=-1&search[limit]=100 -- all E. coli MIC distributions, one row per agent.

lesson: Six attempts proved the values are not in TEXT and I generalised that to 'unobtainable'. The untested axis was whether the URL was addressable with the RIGHT parameter. A wall demonstrated along one axis is not a wall; name the axis you actually tested.
